title: Install Clew
summary: Install Clew, convert supported older ledgers transactionally, and preserve application history and daily scheduling through the product command.

consumers.statement: The authorized local installer and Telete deployment manager.

preconditions.statement: An authorized explicit product selection and required Milieu, Email and Clockwork interfaces are available. Migration of a nonempty schema-one ledger also requires the Platter opportunity reader. Product setup uses ordinary admission; an existing hold can refuse it. The executor adds no dependencies or maintenance holds.

Direct install and recovery require clew/daily-email disabled. They reject an enabled binding and run its disable transition to wait for active processes before runtime publication. They do not select a new definition; select the matching definition before enabling a recovered or updated program.

inputs.statement: Submit ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy clew from the Cell root. CI and Telete are the sole deployment route. --settings ABSOLUTE_JSON supplies private JSON whose clew object contains daily_email_enabled; omission preserves daily intent. Telete freezes settings and owns validation, signed preparation, deployment and the retained outcome. schedule-definition requires existing state and a new absolute output file.

outputs.statement: The selected release contains clew, clew-install and its Chancery provider. The product command initializes empty schema-four state or converts schema one through three transactionally with retained exact retry requests and legacy aliases.

data_semantics.statement: Installation selects programs and initializes or migrates ledger state. It creates no new entries, statuses, or threads. Migration preserves entry IDs, times, sequence, text, corrections, retractions, and original write namespace. Existing jobs receive explicit application-report associations in the external reference model. Platter supplies only schema-one legacy-to-Milieu mappings; schema-two conversion is local.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque UUIDs identify immutable releases; package version, provider contract and database schema are separate identities.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installation performs setup without selected-byte integrity, local ledger integrity, or Milieu snapshot checks. Migration retains its ordinary mapping requirements for every legacy reference. Installation establishes no future availability.

access.statement: The current user owns installation selectors and private ledger state.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Each file-selector replacement is atomic. Failed deployment retains completed file, ledger and schedule changes without automatic retry, rollback or recovery. The product command uses ordinary admission, migrates or initializes state, and retargets the owned daily definition directly while preserving saved or explicit enabled intent and failure incidents. Migration excludes ledger writers and commits schema four, reference associations, aliases and exact write requests in one transaction. Old writers are rejected; frozen email bytes, keys and receipts remain intact.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Clew/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.

operational_limits.statement: There is no completion-time guarantee. Compatible schema-four readers and short SQLite writers can finish across program selection. Migration from schema one through three uses a separate guarded write boundary and preserves all retained entries atomically.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: New releases use cell-install-v4; retained earlier formats remain readable. Only ledger schema four, and email schema one are supported for ordinary use. Contract four supports guarded conversion from ledger schemas one through three. Ordinary commands and direct installation do not migrate state. Recovery requires a matching program and ledger pair; there is no automatic downgrade. Preserve email delivery records.

Schema-three conversion is local and transactionally renames owned job-reference and retry-request fields to Milieu. Retained supplied content, identifiers, order, correction links and frozen delivery evidence stay unchanged. Exact retries use the renamed argument and original write ID.

reliances.statement: Application features require the complete Milieu snapshot reader for first-job admission, job search, and email context. Installation and generic ledger operations do not probe Milieu.

Migration of a nonempty schema-one ledger reads retained Platter opportunities to map each legacy reference to its exact Milieu job ID. Schema-two conversion and generic ledger operations do not read Platter.
Email submits the unchanged payload and stable key to the fixed recipient.
Clockwork activates the installed runner and enforces its shared service-health threshold before new scheduling failure halts.

use_when: Installing, checking or recovering the Clew command and private ledger.
do_not_use_when: Recording an application update or changing Platter preparation.
outcome: Installed Clew commands and provider, with product-owned state setup or migration.
effects: Program deployment selects files and initializes a missing ledger or converts schema one through three to schema four transactionally in place. Existing entry identity, content and exact retry requests remain intact; no thread is invented.

The product command updates its daily definition directly and preserves captured or explicitly supplied enabled intent and failure incidents. Deployment creates no hold, waits for owned scheduled activations before runtime publication, and preserves prior enabled intent.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Clew/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.

Direct install and recovery require clew/daily-email disabled. They reject an enabled binding and run its disable transition to wait for active processes before runtime publication. They do not select a new definition; select the matching definition before enabling a recovered or updated program.
authority: Clew owns its installation and ledger; the shared coordinator owns deployment ordering.
Clockwork owns schedule enforcement; enabling daily_email_enabled explicitly grants standing authority for the Clew digest.
success: Program selection and requested product setup commands complete. Installation does not check artifact integrity, ledger integrity or the Milieu snapshot.
failure_and_recovery: File recovery preserves ledger state and must not claim an incompatible old program can operate schema four. Missing or colliding schema-one mappings stop the upgrade. Preserve current data and unresolved installation evidence. Unsupported or nonempty foreign state fails.

Retain email occurrences, uncertain acceptance and completed deployment effects. The executor stops at failure and performs no automatic retry or product recovery. Inspect current product and schedule state before an authorized new attempt; preserve separately acquired holds and failure incidents.
privacy: Private ledger state is outside source and installation releases.
does_not_authorize: Adding application records, deleting history, immediate test mail, implicit first-time schedule enablement, or approval of a failure halt.
